Build the shared gsm test data bundle

Source: R/build_testdata_bundle.R
build_testdata_bundle.Rd

Generate shared example data and write it to disk with a manifest.json describing the build.

Usage

build_testdata_bundle(
  output_dir,
  config = read_testdata_config(),
  overwrite = FALSE
)

Arguments

output_dir

Directory to write the bundle into. Created if needed.

config

A config list or path to a YAML file; see read_testdata_config(). Defaults to the checked-in config.

overwrite

If FALSE (default), error when output_dir exists and is not empty. If TRUE, delete output_dir and its contents first.

Value

The manifest (a list), invisibly.

Details

The pipeline is:

  1. Simulate raw data with create_longitudinal_study() using the config's seed and parameters.

  2. Set Raw_SITE$site_status to "Active" on every snapshot.

  3. Map each snapshot with gsm.mapping::Ingest() and the gsm.mapping mapping workflows (config domains plus extra_mappings).

  4. Run every gsm.kri metric workflow, including inactive ones (so the example reports show them), and the gsm.qtl metrics.

  5. Run the gsm.reporting workflows, then stamp SnapshotDate from snapshot_dates onto Reporting_Results and Reporting_Bounds.

  6. Combine reporting tables across snapshots and split them by group level.

  7. Write CSVs of the kri0001 and cou0001 analytics (Analysis_Input and Analysis_Summary) from the final snapshot and of the 12 reporting* tables.

  8. Write RDS files of lSource (the final raw snapshot) and of 14 tables read back from those CSVs.

Rows are sorted on explicit keys so identical inputs always produce byte-identical files.

Layout

<output_dir>/
  manifest.json
  analytics{Input,Summary}{,_country}.csv
  reporting{Results,Groups,Bounds,Metrics}{,_country,_study}.csv
  lSource.rds
  analytics{Input,Summary}.rds
  reporting{Results,Groups,Bounds,Metrics}{,_country,_study}.rds

Manifest

fingerprint is a SHA-256 hash over the per-file checksums of the data files only, so two builds with identical data share a fingerprint regardless of built_at, built_by, or workflow_run. package_versions records the installed version (and remote SHA, when available) of each pipeline package.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
build_testdata_bundle("bundle")
} # }
